messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

The team now has departments such as Billing and Technical Support. Let admins create, rename,
and delete groups, and add staff to more than one group. Staff can browse groups and memberships;
groups organize work, they don't hide tickets from other staff.

For example:

```http
POST /api/v1/groups

{"group":{"name":"Billing"}}
```

```http
POST /api/v1/group_memberships

{"group_membership":{"group_id":20,"user_id":12,"default":true}}
```

Use the usual list, detail, and delete routes for both resources, plus PATCH for group names.
List groups and memberships by ID ascending.
Let admins choose a staff member's default with `PUT /group_memberships/:id/make_default`.
Every staff member with memberships should have one default;
removing it should pick another remaining membership.
Filter memberships by `group_id` and `user_id`.

Tickets can now have a `group_id`, with the group's ID/name in `group`, and staff can filter the
inbox by group or `group_id=unassigned`.

An assigned person must belong to the ticket's group. Assigning someone to an ungrouped ticket
should use their default group, if they have one. Moving a ticket to another group should clear
an assignee who doesn't belong there. Clearing the assignee leaves the group in place; explicitly
clearing the group also clears the assignee. Deleting groups or memberships clears invalid assignments.
Suspension keeps memberships for later.

class Account < ApplicationRecord
  CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD = 90.days
  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\z/

  belongs_to :owner, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :processed_inbound_emails, dependent: :delete_all

  has_many :password_reset_tokens, dependent: :delete_all

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip.downcase : value }

  validates :name, presence: true
  validates :subdomain,
    presence: true,
    uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false },
    format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT }

  scope :purge_eligible, -> {
    where.not(cancelled_at: nil).where(cancelled_at: ..CANCELLATION_GRACE_PERIOD.ago)
  }

  def self.register!(account_attrs:, admin_attrs:)
    account = new(
      name: account_attrs[:name],
      subdomain: account_attrs[:subdomain]
    )
    user = User.new(
      account: account,
      name: admin_attrs[:name],
      email: admin_attrs[:email],
      role: "admin",
      verified: false
    )
    raw_password = admin_attrs[:password]
    user.password = raw_password if raw_password.is_a?(String) && raw_password.present?

    account_valid = account.valid?
    user_valid = user.valid?

    unless account_valid && user_valid
      user.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :account
        account.errors.add(:"admin.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(account)
    end

    raw_verification_token = nil

    transaction do
      account.save!
      user.account = account
      user.save!
      account.update!(owner: user)
      raw_verification_token = user.issue_email_verification_token!
    end

    UserMailer.email_verification(user, raw_verification_token).deliver_now

    [account, user]
  end

  def self.purge_cancelled!
    count = 0
    purge_eligible.find_each do |account|
      account.purge!
      count += 1
    end
    count
  end

  def register_customer!(attrs)
    user = users.new(
      name: attrs[:name],
      email: attrs[:email],
      role: "customer",
      verified: false
    )
    raw_password = attrs[:password]
    user.password = raw_password if raw_password.is_a?(String) && raw_password.present?

    raw_verification_token = nil

    with_lock do
      valid = user.valid?
      if user.email.present? && !user.errors.include?(:email) && invitations.pending.exists?(email: user.email)
        user.errors.add(:email, :taken)
        valid = false
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(user) unless valid

      user.save!
      raw_verification_token = user.issue_email_verification_token!
    end

    UserMailer.email_verification(user, raw_verification_token).deliver_now

    user
  end

require "test_helper"
require "rake"

class TeamAndCollaborationTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    ENV.delete("HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL")
    ENV.delete("HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM")
  end

  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def extract_link_params(mail, expected_path)
    body = mail.body.decoded
    match = body.match(%r{(https?://[^\s"<>]+)})
    assert match, "Expected URL in email body, got: #{body.inspect}"
    uri = URI.parse(match[1])
    assert_equal expected_path, uri.path
    [uri, URI.decode_www_form(uri.query).to_h]
  end

  def setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    post "/api/v1/account/create",
      params: {
        account: {
          name: name,
          subdomain: subdomain,
          admin: { name: admin_name, email: email, password: password }
        }
      },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    owner = json_body.fetch("user")
    _uri, query = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: query.fetch("token") } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    owner
  end

  def register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password")
    post "/api/v1/registrations",
      params: { user: { name: name, email: email, password: password } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    _uri, query = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: query.fetch("token") } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    user = json_body.fetch("user")
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    user
  end

  def sign_in!(subdomain:, email:, password:)
    post "/api/v1/sessions",
      params: { session: { email: email, password: password } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    json_body.dig("session", "token")
  end

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)
    {
      "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain,
      "Authorization" => "Bearer #{token}"
    }
  end

  test "invitation lifecycle: create, preview, accept, resend, revoke, expire, filter, ID asc order, and competing email rules" do
    setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    owner_token = sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    owner_headers = auth_headers("acme", owner_token)

    # Admin invites Sam as agent
    assert_difference -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }, 1 do
      post "/api/v1/invitations",
        params: { invitation: { email: "  SAM@Example.Test ", role: "agent" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
    end
    assert_response :created

    sam_invite = json_body.fetch("invitation")
    assert_kind_of Integer, sam_invite["id"]
    assert_equal "sam@example.test", sam_invite["email"]
    assert_equal "agent", sam_invite["role"]
    assert_equal "pending", sam_invite["status"]
    assert sam_invite["expires_at"].present?
    assert_nil sam_invite["accepted_at"]

    assert_not sam_invite.key?("token")
    assert_not sam_invite.key?("token_digest")

    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_equal ["sam@example.test"], mail.to

    first_sam_token = query.fetch("token")
    assert first_sam_token.present?

    # Competing pending invitation for same email is rejected and sends no email
    assert_no_difference [-> { Invitation.count }, -> { ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.size }] do

    assert_equal 3, json_body["count"]

  test "customers can filter their own requests by status with pagination, without seeing other customers or internal priority" do
    setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    owner_headers = auth_headers("acme", sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password"))

    register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test")
    register_and_verify_customer!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Blake", email: "blake@example.test")

    avery_headers = auth_headers("acme", sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password"))
    blake_headers = auth_headers("acme", sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "blake@example.test", password: "my-customer-password"))

    # Staff cannot use customer /requests endpoint
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open" }, headers: owner_headers
    assert_response :forbidden

    # Avery creates 4 requests (2 will stay open, 1 pending, 1 solved); Blake creates 1 open request
    post "/api/v1/requests",
      params: { request: { subject: "Avery Open 1", comment: { body: "Still open 1" } } },
      headers: avery_headers,
      as: :json
    r_open_1 = json_body.dig("request", "id")

    r_open_2 = nil
    travel 30.seconds do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Open 2", comment: { body: "Still open 2" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_open_2 = json_body.dig("request", "id")
    end

    r_pending = nil
    travel 1.minute do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Pending", comment: { body: "Waiting" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_pending = json_body.dig("request", "id")
    end

    r_solved = nil
    travel 2.minutes do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Avery Solved", comment: { body: "Done" } } },
        headers: avery_headers,
        as: :json
      r_solved = json_body.dig("request", "id")
    end

    travel 3.minutes do
      post "/api/v1/requests",
        params: { request: { subject: "Blake Open", comment: { body: "Blake body" } } },
        headers: blake_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :created
    end

    # Staff sets statuses and marks r_open_1 as high priority
    travel 4.minutes do
      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r_open_1}",
        params: { ticket: { priority: "high" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok

      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r_pending}",
        params: { ticket: { status: "pending" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok

      patch "/api/v1/tickets/#{r_solved}",
        params: { ticket: { status: "solved" } },
        headers: owner_headers,
        as: :json
      assert_response :ok
    end

    # Avery filters own requests by status (and priority bump on r_open_1 did NOT move it ahead of r_open_2!)
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal [r_open_2, r_open_1], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }
    json_body.fetch("requests").each { |r| assert_not r.key?("priority") }

    # Pagination with status filter on /requests
    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open", page: 1, per_page: 1 }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]
    assert_equal [r_open_2], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "pending" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [r_pending], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "solved" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [r_solved], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "open", page: 1, per_page: 1 }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 2, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]
    assert_equal [r_open_2], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "pending" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [r_pending], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: "solved" }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal [r_solved], json_body.fetch("requests").map { |r| r["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/requests?status=", headers: avery_headers

    assert_equal 4, json_body["count"]

    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    get "/api/v1/requests", params: { status: ["open"] }, headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :unprocessable_content
  end

First, multi-tenancy is crucial. Each `Group` and `GroupMembership` *must* belong to an `Account`, and these relationships need to cascade appropriately on deletion to maintain data integrity. The `Account` model's associations are critical here, and the cascading delete ensures a clean purge if an account is cancelled. We need to implement the account-level security checks: `X-Helpdesk-Account`, `authenticate_user!`, and `require_active_account!` must be enforced across all relevant endpoints. A cancelled account should result in a 403 Forbidden error, and a missing or invalid account identifier should trigger the appropriate 400 or 404 responses.  Unauthenticated users get 401.

Next, permissions: We are explicitly told that admins can do *everything* and staff can only browse. So, we need to carefully define the roles and permissions for each action: creating, renaming, deleting groups, adding members, and making a default membership. The `GroupsController` and `GroupMembershipsController` need to be meticulously implemented, with `require_admin!` protecting create, update, and destroy actions, and `require_staff!` for index and show. The `/make_default` route on `GroupMembershipsController` should accept both PUT and PATCH and also require `require_admin!`. What about customers? They should get a 403 Forbidden for all the endpoints related to groups and group memberships. Crucially, the internal `group_id` should *never* be exposed to the customer.

Now, let's zoom in on the `Group` resource:

    *   The `Group` model has: `account_id` (bigint, not null), `name` (string, not null), and timestamp attributes.

    *   **Uniqueness Validation:** Group names *must* be unique within an account, but not across accounts. Case-insensitive uniqueness is essential to maintain data integrity and consistency. We need to ensure that the database enforces this constraint using a unique functional index (`account_id`, `LOWER(name)`) which requires we use case-insensitive uniqueness with `scope: :account_id` and the database index.

Now, we need to consider edge cases and error handling:
*   We will ensure the name is a string, and not `nil`, a number, or an empty string. If non-string is passed, we expect the controller's `scalar_string()` method to return `nil`. A `nil` value or a missing `:name` key in a `PATCH` request should result in validation errors and a 422 Unprocessable Entity response.

            error: "Email can't be blank",
            errors: { email: ["can't be blank"] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_content
          return
        end

        user = current_account.users.find_by(email: email)
        if user && !user.suspended?
          raw_token = user.issue_password_reset_token!
          UserMailer.password_reset(user, raw_token).deliver_now
        end

        render json: { password_reset: { status: "ok" } }, status: :ok
      end

      def confirm
        pr_params = require_object_param(:password_reset)
        raw_token = scalar_string(pr_params[:token])
        new_password = scalar_string(pr_params[:password])
        token_record = PasswordResetToken.find_valid_for_account(current_account, raw_token)

        if token_record.nil? || token_record.user.suspended?
          render json: {
            error: "Invalid or expired password reset token",
            errors: { token: ["is invalid or expired"] }
          }, status: :unprocessable_content
          return
        end

        user = token_record.user
        user.change_password!(new_password)

        render json: { user: user.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end
    end
  end
end

**Analyzing API Conventions and JSON Serialization**

Okay, so I'm looking at these different `DELETE` requests and immediately see the divergence in behavior. Destroying a session (`DELETE /api/v1/session`) versus soft-revoking an invitation (`DELETE /api/v1/invitations/:id`). That's standard practice: when you *actually* remove a record, you should be returning `204 No Content` as per REST and Rails API conventions. So, for `DELETE /api/v1/groups/:id` and `DELETE /api/v1/group_memberships/:id`, a `204` is the correct response because the record is truly gone. We’ve established that it is indeed standard Rails API behavior to return `204 No Content` when deleting something like a `Group` or `GroupMembership`.

Now, let's move on to the JSON serialization formats. I've got a good handle on the patterns. I need to make sure that the `Group` and `GroupMembership` serialization adheres to the established conventions. Let's start by mapping them:

*   `Account#as_api_json`: Straightforward, standard fields.
*   `User#as_api_json`: Similar, includes `account_id`, which is a key pattern.
*   `Invitation#as_api_json`: Following the same format:  `account_id`, `id` and `created_at` etc.
*   `Ticket#as_ticket_json`: A bit more complex, with nested `requester` and `assignee` objects, but still clear.

Now, for `Group`: it's all about consistent field names. The proposed `group.as_api_json` includes `id`, `account_id`, `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. This fits the patterns we've seen: `id`, `account_id`, `name`, `created_at`, `updated_at` aligns with both the `User` and `Invitation` formats.

For `GroupMembership`: We need to determine if we should be including nested group or user objects. It looks like the presence of nested objects is explicitly defined, and the example in the `Ticket` description states explicitly when you should. `Invitation` uses `invited_by_id`, so it probably won't use the nested object. Now, let’s check the tests. I need to know how thoroughly the tests check the complete JSON structure versus individual keys. This will help determine if we need to change how we present the data in the output or not. I'll search for `as_api_json` keys and specific resource names in the integration tests. This will make certain the implementation and the tests align to the intended patterns.

messages.content: Let's check all `patch` test cases in `test/integration/` to see how empty objects `{}` on `PATCH` are tested.
messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive: Architectural Clarity & Business Rule Enforcement**

Alright, let's break this down. Seeing the patterns in `Ticket#as_ticket_json` clarifies the design. The nested `assignee` and `requester` in the ticket format directly map to what's expected with `group`, based on the prompt's explicit requirement of including the group's ID and name. The nil handling for `group_id` mirrors the established pattern for `assignee_id`, reinforcing consistency. With the group name being dynamically serialized from the `Group` record, updating the group's name will auto-reflect on the tickets.

Now, considering `GroupMembership#as_api_json`, the design choices become critical. Do we nest `group` or `user`? The answer is "no," because the existing architecture (particularly `Invitation`, `Account`, and the integration tests) avoids nesting unless explicitly requested, and here it isn't. The prompt's lack of a specific "ID/name in group" directive for memberships, contrasts sharply with the explicit directive for tickets. Also, unlike the specific fields on a ticket, a `GroupMembership` could expose differing fields on a `User`, and we would have to decide which to expose for the API, where `User`'s staff JSON has different fields than its API JSON. So the cleanest approach is to keep the nested data out of the `GroupMembership` object, making it consistent with other API objects.

Now, let's meticulously dissect the business rules and potential edge cases for groups.

*   **Group CRUD (`POST`, `GET`, `GET /:id`, `PATCH/PUT /:id`, `DELETE /:id`)**:

    *   **Create (POST)**: Admin-only, with a clear `403` for non-admins. The `name` validation is rigorous, ensuring it's a string, stripped of whitespace, and unique within the account. Duplicates across accounts are permitted. A `201` with the created group's JSON is returned.
    *   **List (GET)**: Staff-accessible, scoped to the account, and ID-ordered, with pagination.
    *   **Detail (GET /:id)**: Staff-accessible, with a careful lookup ensuring the ID exists and belongs to the account. Invalid IDs or cross-account lookups result in a `404`.
    *   **Update (PATCH/PUT)**: Admin-only, with the lookup done *before* access checks, to maintain consistency. The code *should* be checking the presence of a group name in the params, because a missing name is an attempt to update to something blank, or change nothing, and the existing test framework for profiles does this. We need to check if the framework already includes this, and if not, add a test to see that `{}` gives a `200` (nothing is changed) or `422` (blank name). The only field that can be updated is the `name`.

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Group Deletion and Ticket Assignments**

Okay, let's break this down. First, I'm noting the consistency in how we handle `update` actions across different controllers. The pattern in `UsersController#update`, `TicketsController#update`, and `GroupsController#update` is clear: validate parameters, and apply the updates safely. Empty parameters don't cause crashes, but return a `422`. Good.

Now, the main focus is on the group deletion (`DELETE /api/v1/groups/:id`) and its effects. We've got two key effects to consider. First, *memberships*: When a group is deleted, any staff member whose *default* group is the deleted one must have another remaining membership promoted to become their default. Excellent, because the SQL `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `group_memberships.group_id` alone *wouldn't* handle this, leaving staff potentially without a default. I'll need to write a test case to explicitly verify this promotion.

Second, let's turn our attention to the *tickets*. The requirement is that "Deleting groups or memberships clears invalid assignments." Now, that sounds simple, but a closer examination reveals subtleties. Tickets can now have a group, and assignees. The key question is: What should happen to a ticket's `group_id` and `assignee_id` when the ticket's group gets deleted?

We're told explicitly that "explicitly clearing the group also clears the assignee." This is critical. But it also states that "an assigned person must belong to the ticket's group." This sets up an *invariant*: If a ticket has both a `group_id` and an `assignee_id`, the assignee *must* be a member of that group. And, of course, the assignee must be `active_staff`.

There are two possibilities for group-assignee interactions with the delete action. Firstly, consider the case where the group is explicitly cleared, i.e., `group_id: nil`. In this case, both the group and assignee *must* be cleared. The system must clear the ticket's `group_id` *and* the ticket's `assignee_id`.

Secondly, consider the general case: what happens to `assignee_id` when the `group_id` is removed because the group has been deleted? When deleting a group, we have this general statement: "Deleting groups or memberships clears invalid assignments." What precisely does this mean? We need to verify that "invalid" here means the group, which the ticket is assigned to, no longer exists, and so the assigned person must also be unassigned (i.e. also set to `nil`).

Now, let's analyze the edge cases:

*   **Ungrouped Tickets:** The prompt states "Assigning someone to an ungrouped ticket should use their default group, if they have one." This is straightforward. However, what if there's *no* default group for the staff member? Existing tests do this already! If a staff member has no group, they can still be assigned to a ticket. In these cases, it has to be allowed that tickets have `assignee_id` when `group_id` is `nil`.

*   **Patching an Ungrouped Ticket:** So, in summary: if a ticket is ungrouped (`group_id: nil`) and you patch it with `assignee_id: sam["id"]` and Sam has *no* group, the patch must be allowed. If the ticket is ungrouped and you patch it with `assignee_id: sam["id"]`, and Sam *has* groups, the ticket must be assigned Sam's default group.

*   **Assignee Does Not Belong:** If a ticket is patched with a new `group_id` AND the assignee does not belong to that group, the request must return `422 Unprocessable Content`.

With all of this in mind, and based on the invariants, it is clear that when deleting a group that a ticket belongs to, we must set both the `group_id` and `assignee_id` on the ticket to `nil`. We need tests to ensure these actions.

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing Group and User Assignment Logic**

Okay, let's break this down. That grep output has me focused, so let's carefully re-examine this problem. We're looking at how group assignments and user assignments intertwine, especially in the context of deleting groups or memberships. The prompt's language is precise, and it's key to understanding the intended behavior.

First, I see the core concept: a ticket's group dictates its allowed assignees. If someone's assigned, they *must* belong to the ticket's group. Conversely, a staff member assigned to an ungrouped ticket will have their *default* group applied (if one exists). The prompt makes this explicit.

Now, let's dig into the *implications* of group deletion. If a group is deleted, what happens? Let's consider a scenario: a ticket, "T," is assigned to "Billing," and "Sam" is the assignee. If "Billing" is deleted, should Sam remain assigned? And let's not get ahead of ourselves and examine all the possibilities.

1.  Why was Ticket T assigned to Sam when it was assigned to Billing? Because Sam had membership to Billing!
2.  Even more important: if Sam also belongs to *Technical Support*? In this case, Ticket T might have a group ID of nil and be assigned to Sam, but Sam is assigned to Tech Support with default: true!

    *   An assigned person must belong to the ticket's group.
    *   Assigning someone to an ungrouped ticket should use their default group, if they have one.
    *   *So, if someone has a default group they'll be assigned to that group, if not it can be unassigned!*

    So if a ticket is assigned to a user who has a group, then the ticket needs a group! If a ticket doesn't have a group, then you can assign the user with `PATCH /api/v1/tickets/:id` if the user doesn't have a group.

    *   If Ticket has `group_id: nil`, and you send `PATCH /tickets/:id { ticket: { assignee_id: sam.id } }`:
        "Assigning someone to an ungrouped ticket should use their default group, if they have one." -> Ticket gets `group_id: sam_default_group.id, assignee_id: sam.id`!
    *   If Ticket has `group_id: billing.id, assignee_id: sam.id`, and you send `PATCH /tickets/:id { ticket: { group_id: nil } }`:
        "explicitly clearing the group also clears the assignee." -> Ticket gets `group_id: nil, assignee_id: nil`!
    *   What if you send `PATCH /tickets/:id { ticket: { group_id: nil, assignee_id: sam.id } }` in the SAME request?
        If someone explicitly sets `group_id: nil` AND `assignee_id: sam.id` in the same request.
        When `group_id` is explicitly `nil`, "explicitly clearing the group also clears the assignee" OR "An assigned person must belong to the ticket's group" -> we'll check that case carefully too!

And the critical part: *how does "deleting groups or memberships clears invalid assignments" fit in?*

Let's break this into cases:

*   **Deleting a membership:** Ticket T (`group_id = Billing, assignee_id = Sam`). If we delete Sam's membership in Billing, Ticket T's `group_id` stays "Billing". However, Sam is no longer a valid assignee. The "group assignment" is now invalid, so `assignee_id` becomes `nil`.

*   **Deleting a group:** Ticket T (`group_id = Billing, assignee_id = Sam`). And Ticket T_unassigned (`group_id = Billing, assignee_id = nil`). If Group "Billing" is deleted, `group_id` *must* become `nil` on *both* tickets. But what happens to the assignee?

**STOP! Let's carefully reread the prompt!** We must analyze what "clears invalid assignments" means in the context of both membership and group deletion.

**A Deep Dive into Ticket Grouping and Assignment**

Okay, here's the mental model I've constructed based on the prompt, drawing heavily from my Zendesk/Helpdesk experience, and this codebase. This is a very clear and well-defined system.

My understanding is that a ticket has two key assignment fields: `group_id` for group assignment and `assignee_id` for agent assignment. The system operates in this way:

1.  **Assigning to an Ungrouped Ticket:** If you assign a person to a ticket that doesn't belong to any group (`group_id == nil`), and if that person *has* a default group, then the ticket's `group_id` is automatically set to their default group. If they have *no* group memberships, the `group_id` remains `nil`, but the `assignee_id` is set to that person.

2.  **Assigning to a Grouped Ticket:** If you assign someone to a ticket already assigned to a group (`group_id != nil`), the person *must* belong to that group. This is a crucial validation point; if they don't, it's an error (`422 Unprocessable Content`).

3.  **Moving a Ticket Between Groups:** When a ticket is moved to a new group (by setting `group_id` to a new `other_group_id`), the system carefully evaluates the current assignee:
    *   If the assignee is a member of the *new* group, the `assignee_id` *stays* in place.
    *   If the assignee is *not* a member of the new group, the `assignee_id` is cleared (set to `nil`). This is essential for maintaining valid group-agent associations.

4.  **Clearing the Assignee:** When the assignee is explicitly cleared (by setting `assignee_id` to `nil` without also setting `group_id`), the `assignee_id` becomes `nil`, *but* the `group_id` *remains* in place. This preserves the ticket's group assignment.

5.  **Explicitly Clearing the Group:** Now, this is where it's interesting! If the group is explicitly cleared (by setting `group_id` to `nil` without also setting `assignee_id`), *both* the `group_id` and `assignee_id` are cleared (set to `nil`). Think of it as a complete unassignment. (Wait: why would anyone pass `{ group_id: null, assignee_id: user_id }`? We will analyze `{ group_id: ..., assignee_id: ... }` combinations right below!)

6.  **Deleting Groups or Memberships:** This is where the cleanup occurs:

    *   **Deleting a Group (`DELETE /groups/:id`):** When a group (e.g., "Billing") is deleted, all tickets that were assigned to that group *must* have *both* `group_id` and `assignee_id` cleared (set to `nil`). This makes total sense! If the group is gone, the tickets are no longer associated with it, and any agent assigned to that group is also unassigned.
    *   **Deleting a Membership (`DELETE /group_memberships/:id`):** If a GroupMembership (e.g., `(Billing, Sam)`) is deleted, any ticket assigned *both* to that group *and* to that user (Sam) will have `assignee_id` set to `nil` (and only `assignee_id`). This cleanup makes sure `Billing` stays in place, but that Sam is no longer assigned to those tickets.

    In my mind, these actions (deleting groups and memberships) are explicitly implemented to avoid invalid assignments.

7.  **User Suspension:** When a user is suspended, the system behaves in a very specific way:

    *   The `group_memberships` are *kept*, and `group_id` stays in place!
    *   Any tickets assigned to the suspended user will have `assignee_id` set to `nil`.

    This design means that suspending a user doesn't cause a loss of group association, which is crucial for data integrity. Note the use of `.update_all()` in this step: that means that the `updated_at` and `customer_updated_at` fields should not be touched, so those fields keep their original ordering.

    It's all about ensuring that ticket assignments are valid and consistent with the current state of groups, memberships, and users.

**Okay, here’s my understanding of how I’d implement these group and assignment features, focusing on the key design decisions and invariants.**

My primary objective is to make assignment management as seamless, logical, and consistent as possible. I want to avoid introducing any unexpected edge cases or contradictions. I’m thinking about this in terms of *states* of a `Ticket` and `User` in relation to groups, and *state transitions* based on API calls.

1.  **Group and Membership Models**:
    *   I’ll start with the database schema and indexes. The core is the `Group` and `GroupMembership` tables. I will use a case-insensitive unique index on the group name within an account to prevent duplicate group names. I need to enforce a *single* default group per user with a partial unique index, which is super important! The `on_delete: :cascade` foreign key ensures complete data integrity when a user, group or account is deleted.
2.  **API Endpoints & Controller Logic**:
    *   **Group Management (`GroupsController`):** I’ll create the standard CRUD endpoints for groups. The critical part is the case-insensitive uniqueness check for group names, to avoid conflicts, and I also want to make sure the name doesn't contain a NUL byte.
    *   **Membership Management (`GroupMembershipsController`):** This is where it gets complex. The `create` action needs careful validation: User must be staff in the account, a user can't be added to the same group twice, default parameter validation (boolean only), and proper handling of the *default* group invariant. The `make_default` action will transition the default group by `PUT /group_memberships/:id/make_default` and *must* clear all other default memberships for that user. The `destroy` action (`DELETE /group_memberships/:id`) requires careful handling of the default membership; removing the default requires another group membership to be assigned as the new default; plus it needs to clear the `assignee_id` from all tickets *in that group*.
    *   **Ticket Updates (`TicketsController`):** Here, I’m focused on updating logic. I’ll make sure that changing the group on a ticket (or clearing it) *also* clears the assignee if the assignee is not in the new (or any) group and that the logic correctly implements state transitions described in the prompt. I will also make sure that I don't break customers' functionality by changing group ID's in the background.

3.  **Core Invariants and Rules**:
    *   **Default Group Invariant:** Every staff member with at least one group membership *must* have one default group. Removing the default must automatically assign the next earliest membership as the default.
    *   **Assignment to Group Rule:** An assigned staff member *must* be a member of the ticket's group, or the assignment is invalid.
    *   **Group Deletion/Membership Removal Rule:** Deleting a group, or removing a user from a group, should clear the assignee on *all* tickets belonging to the group, but *not* affect the assignee on tickets in other groups. Also, I must ensure this rule properly works on concurrent operations with a pessimistic lock.
    *   **Ticket State Transitions**: I’ve defined every valid Ticket state based on group and assignee assignment, and I’ll make sure all state transitions (via `PATCH /tickets/:id`) respect this. For example, explicitly setting `group_id: nil, assignee_id: staff_member.id` is valid *only* when the staff member has no other groups.

4.  **Error Handling**: I’ll design errors to be very precise. I will include a detailed error message that provides information on *why* a request fails, with specific error messages for missing, invalid, or conflicting parameters. The `422 Unprocessable Content` status code will be used extensively for validation failures, which includes a detailed `errors` hash.

5.  **Concurrency Safety**: I’m employing `account.with_lock` to prevent race conditions during membership updates, group updates, and assignment changes. The whole state of the system relies on it.

6.  **Database Design**: A complete table schema with foreign keys, null constraints, and appropriate indexes to optimize lookups.

I’m meticulously verifying *every* combination of parameters in `PATCH /tickets/:id` (group, assignee, null, and non-null) in a comprehensive truth table. I’m thinking about edge cases: concurrent operations, invalid inputs, and every state a ticket can be in.

The goal is to provide a clean and intuitive API, along with a solid, bug-free implementation. Every check I’m making ensures the system behaves as expected, with zero surprises

Next, I need to meticulously scrutinize `Ticket#apply_staff_update!`. Here's where the nuance kicks in. The `reload` call inside `account.with_lock` is the critical point. Let's trace it carefully.

Imagine someone calls `@ticket.apply_staff_update!(...)` and it throws an `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid` – it happens. Inside `account.with_lock`, `reload` clears the existing errors, then sets attributes, validates, populates `self.errors`, and then raises the exception. But… does the exception keep those errors?

Yes! The transaction rollback *doesn't* clear the `errors` on the in-memory object! This is crucial. ActiveRecord's transaction rollback preserves those errors on the record itself, which means our `BaseController#render_record_invalid` will correctly display those validation errors. This is crucial for consistency, and I need to check all of the methods that raise an exception this way. Specifically, `Account.register!`, `Account#register_customer!`, `Invitation.issue!`, `Invitation#resend!`, `Invitation#revoke!`, `User#apply_admin_update!` should also follow this pattern.

And, what about that `reply_comment` for `TicketMailer.staff_reply`? Instead of relying on an instance variable, the local variable `reply_comment_to_deliver = nil` will be declared *before* the `account.with_lock` block. We'll set it inside the block right after `save!` and then send the email *after* the `account.with_lock` block is done. `TicketMailer.staff_reply(self, reply_comment_to_deliver).deliver_now if reply_comment_to_deliver`. Clean, thread-safe, and avoids polluting instance variables.

When we `reload` `@ticket`, those cached associations get cleared. After `apply_staff_update!` returns, `@ticket.as_ticket_json` accesses those attributes, which is fine because `reload` reloads the relationships we need for rendering the ticket details, using just one query on the `PATCH` action.

class Group < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  has_many :group_memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :users, through: :group_memberships
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :nullify

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }

  validates :name,
    presence: true,
    format: { without: /\u0000/ },
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }

  scope :ordered, -> { order(id: :asc) }

  def self.create_for_account!(account:, name:)
    group = account.groups.new(name: name)

    account.with_lock do
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(group) unless group.valid?
      group.save!
    end

    group
  end

  def rename!(new_name)
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      self.name = new_name
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self) unless valid?
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def destroy_with_cleanup!
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      affected_user_ids = group_memberships.where(default: true).pluck(:user_id)

      account.tickets.where(group_id: id).update_all(group_id: nil, assignee_id: nil)
      group_memberships.delete_all
      destroy!

      affected_user_ids.each do |uid|
        next if account.group_memberships.where(user_id: uid, default: true).exists?

        replacement = account.group_memberships.where(user_id: uid).ordered.first
        replacement&.update!(default: true)
      end
    end
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      account_id: account_id,
      name: name,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end
EOF

class GroupMembership < ApplicationRecord
  MAX_BIGINT = (1 << 63) - 1

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :group
  belongs_to :user

  validates :default, inclusion: { in: [true, false] }
  validates :user_id, uniqueness: { scope: :group_id }

  scope :ordered, -> { order(id: :asc) }

  def self.add_member!(account:, raw_group_id:, raw_user_id:, has_default:, default_value:)
    membership = account.group_memberships.new

    account.with_lock do
      group = resolve_group(account, raw_group_id, membership)
      user = resolve_staff_user(account, raw_user_id, membership)

      if has_default && default_value.nil?
        membership.default = nil
        membership.errors.add(:default, :inclusion)
      end

      if group && user && account.group_memberships.exists?(group_id: group.id, user_id: user.id)
        membership.errors.add(:user_id, :taken)
      end

      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(membership) if membership.errors.any?

      existing_default = account.group_memberships.where(user_id: user.id, default: true).exists?
      make_default = if !existing_default
        true
      elsif has_default
        default_value
      else
        false
      end

      if make_default && existing_default
        account.group_memberships.where(user_id: user.id, default: true).update_all(
          default: false,
          updated_at: Time.current
        )
      end

      membership.group = group
      membership.user = user
      membership.default = make_default
      membership.save!
    end

    membership
  end

  def make_default!
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      unless default?
        account.group_memberships
          .where(user_id: user_id, default: true)
          .where.not(id: id)
          .update_all(default: false, updated_at: Time.current)
        update!(default: true)
      end
    end

    self
  end

  def destroy_with_cleanup!
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      uid = user_id
      gid = group_id
      was_default = default?

      account.tickets.where(group_id: gid, assignee_id: uid).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
      destroy!

      if was_default && !account.group_memberships.where(user_id: uid, default: true).exists?
        replacement = account.group_memberships.where(user_id: uid).ordered.first
        replacement&.update!(default: true)
      end
    end
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      account_id: account_id,
      group_id: group_id,
      user_id: user_id,
      default: self.default,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  def self.parse_id(raw_id)
    id = if raw_id.is_a?(String)
      return nil unless /\A\d+\z/.match?(raw_id)
      raw_id.to_i
    elsif raw_id.is_a?(Integer)
      raw_id
    end
    return nil unless id && id >= 1 && id <= MAX_BIGINT

    id
  end

  def self.resolve_group(account, raw_group_id, membership)
    if raw_group_id.nil? || raw_group_id == ""
      membership.errors.add(:group_id, :blank)
      return nil
    end

    parsed_id = parse_id(raw_group_id)
    group = parsed_id && account.groups.find_by(id: parsed_id)
    unless group
      membership.errors.add(:group_id, :invalid)
      return nil
    end

    group
  end
  private_class_method :resolve_group

  def self.resolve_staff_user(account, raw_user_id, membership)
    if raw_user_id.nil? || raw_user_id == ""
      membership.errors.add(:user_id, :blank)
      return nil
    end

    parsed_id = parse_id(raw_user_id)
    user = parsed_id && account.users.find_by(id: parsed_id)
    unless user && user.staff?
      membership.errors.add(:user_id, :invalid)
      return nil
    end

    user
  end
  private_class_method :resolve_staff_user
end
EOF

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  class InvalidEmailDelivery < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  MAX_BIGINT = (1 << 63) - 1

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :group, optional: true
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :processed_inbound_emails, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :comments, dependent: :delete_all

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }

  before_validation :ensure_reply_token, on: :create
  before_create :ensure_customer_updated_at

  validates :subject, presence: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, presence: true, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validates :reply_token, presence: true, uniqueness: true

  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :customer_recently_active, -> { order(customer_updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :matching_query, ->(raw_query) {
    query = raw_query.to_s
    if query.empty?
      all
    elsif query.include?("\u0000")
      none
    else
      pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(query, "\\")}%"
      where(
        <<~'SQL'.squish,
          tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'
          OR EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM comments
            WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id
              AND comments.account_id = tickets.account_id
              AND comments.public = TRUE
              AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern ESCAPE '\'
          )
        SQL
        pattern: pattern
      )
    end
  }

  def self.open_request!(account:, requester:, subject:, comment_body:)
    now = Time.current
    ticket = new(
      account: account,
      requester: requester,
      subject: subject,
      status: "open",
      priority: "normal",
      email_origin: false,
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now,
      customer_updated_at: now
    )
    comment = Comment.new(
      account: account,
      ticket: ticket,
      author: requester,
      body: comment_body,
      public: true,
      created_at: now,
      updated_at: now
    )

    ticket_valid = ticket.valid?
    comment_valid = comment.valid?

    unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        ticket.errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(ticket)
    end

    transaction do
      ticket.save!
      comment.ticket = ticket
      comment.save!
    end

    ticket
  end

  def self.open_from_email!(
    account:,
    sender_email:,
    sender_name:,
    subject:,
    body:,
    dedup_message_id:,
    header_message_id:
  )
    normalized_email = sender_email.to_s.strip.downcase
    cleaned_subject = subject.to_s.strip
    cleaned_body = body.to_s.strip

    return nil if normalized_email.empty? || cleaned_subject.empty? || cleaned_body.empty?
    return :duplicate if ProcessedInboundEmail.exists?(message_id: dedup_message_id)

    outcome = nil
    created_ticket = nil
    requester = nil
    raw_verification_token = nil

    transaction do
      account.with_lock do
        account.reload
        raise InvalidEmailDelivery unless account.active?

        if ProcessedInboundEmail.exists?(message_id: dedup_message_id)
          outcome = :duplicate
        else
          existing_user = account.users.find_by(email: normalized_email)
          requester = if existing_user
            raise InvalidEmailDelivery unless existing_user.customer? && !existing_user.suspended?
            existing_user
          else
            raise InvalidEmailDelivery if account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: normalized_email)

            fallback_name = normalized_email.split("@").first.to_s.strip
            customer_name = sender_name.to_s.delete("\u0000").strip
            customer_name = fallback_name.empty? ? normalized_email : fallback_name if customer_name.empty?

            new_user = account.users.new(
              name: customer_name,
              email: normalized_email,
              role: "customer",
              verified: false,
              suspended: false
            )
            new_user.password = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(32)
            new_user.save!
            raw_verification_token = new_user.issue_email_verification_token!
            new_user
          end

          now = Time.current
          ticket = new(
            account: account,
            requester: requester,
            subject: cleaned_subject,
            status: "open",
            priority: "normal",
            email_origin: true,
            email_message_id: header_message_id,
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now,
            customer_updated_at: now
          )
          comment = Comment.new(
            account: account,
            ticket: ticket,
            author: requester,
            body: cleaned_body,
            public: true,
            created_at: now,
            updated_at: now
          )
          raise InvalidEmailDelivery unless ticket.valid? && comment.valid?

          ticket.save!
          comment.ticket = ticket
          comment.save!
          ProcessedInboundEmail.create!(
            account: account,
            ticket: ticket,
            comment: comment,
            message_id: dedup_message_id
          )

          created_ticket = ticket
          outcome = :created
        end
      end
    end

    if outcome == :created && raw_verification_token
      UserMailer.email_verification(requester, raw_verification_token).deliver_now
    end

    outcome == :duplicate ? :duplicate : created_ticket
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    :duplicate
  rescue InvalidEmailDelivery, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    nil
  end

  def reply_from_email!(sender_email:, body:, dedup_message_id:, header_message_id:)
    normalized_email = sender_email.to_s.strip.downcase
    cleaned_body = body.to_s.strip

    return nil if normalized_email.empty? || cleaned_body.empty?
    return :duplicate if ProcessedInboundEmail.exists?(message_id: dedup_message_id)

    outcome = nil
    created_comment = nil

    self.class.transaction do
      account.with_lock do
        account.reload
        raise InvalidEmailDelivery unless account.active?

        with_lock do
          if ProcessedInboundEmail.exists?(message_id: dedup_message_id)
            outcome = :duplicate
          else
            req = account.users.find_by(id: requester_id)
            raise InvalidEmailDelivery unless req && req.customer? && !req.suspended? && req.email == normalized_email

            now = Time.current
            comment = Comment.new(
              account: account,
              ticket: self,
              author: req,
              body: cleaned_body,
              public: true,
              created_at: now,
              updated_at: now
            )
            raise InvalidEmailDelivery unless comment.valid?

            comment.save!
            self.status = "open"
            self.updated_at = now
            self.customer_updated_at = now
            self.email_message_id = header_message_id if header_message_id.present?
            save!

            ProcessedInboundEmail.create!(
              account: account,
              ticket: self,
              comment: comment,
              message_id: dedup_message_id
            )

            created_comment = comment
            outcome = :replied
          end
        end
      end
    end

    outcome == :duplicate ? :duplicate : created_comment
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    :duplicate
  rescue InvalidEmailDelivery, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    nil
  end

  def reply_address
    "#{account.subdomain}+#{reply_token}@#{HelpdeskConfig.support_domain}"
  end

  def apply_staff_update!(
    author:,
    has_comment:,
    comment_attrs:,
    has_status:,
    status:,
    has_assignee: false,
    raw_assignee_id: nil,
    has_priority: false,
    priority: nil,
    has_group: false,
    raw_group_id: nil
  )
    unless has_comment || has_status || has_assignee || has_priority || has_group
      errors.add(:base, "Comment, status, assignee, priority, or group is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    reply_comment_to_deliver = nil

    account.with_lock do
      reload
      self.status = status if has_status
      self.priority = priority if has_priority

      group_invalid = false
      target_group = self.group
      if has_group
        if raw_group_id.nil?
          target_group = nil
        else
          parsed_group_id = parse_record_id_value(raw_group_id)
          found_group = parsed_group_id && account.groups.find_by(id: parsed_group_id)
          if found_group
            target_group = found_group
          else
            group_invalid = true
          end
        end
      end

      assignee_invalid = false
      target_assignee = self.assignee
      if has_assignee
        if raw_assignee_id.nil?
          target_assignee = nil
        else
          parsed_assignee_id = parse_record_id_value(raw_assignee_id)
          staff_member = parsed_assignee_id && account.users.active_staff.find_by(id: parsed_assignee_id)
          if staff_member
            target_assignee = staff_member
          else
            assignee_invalid = true
          end
        end
      end

      assignee_group_mismatch = false
      unless group_invalid || assignee_invalid
        if has_group && has_assignee
          if target_group.nil?
            if target_assignee && account.group_memberships.exists?(user_id: target_assignee.id)
              assignee_group_mismatch = true
            else
              self.group = nil
              self.assignee = target_assignee
            end
          else
            if target_assignee.nil?
              self.group = target_group
              self.assignee = nil
            elsif account.group_memberships.exists?(group_id: target_group.id, user_id: target_assignee.id)
              self.group = target_group
              self.assignee = target_assignee
            else
              assignee_group_mismatch = true
            end
          end
        elsif has_group
          if target_group.nil?
            self.group = nil
            self.assignee = nil
          else
            self.group = target_group
            if self.assignee_id.present? && !account.group_memberships.exists?(group_id: target_group.id, user_id: self.assignee_id)
              self.assignee = nil
            end
          end
        elsif has_assignee
          if target_assignee.nil?
            self.assignee = nil
          elsif self.group_id.nil?
            default_membership = account.group_memberships.includes(:group).find_by(user_id: target_assignee.id, default: true)
            self.assignee = target_assignee
            self.group = default_membership.group if default_membership
          elsif account.group_memberships.exists?(group_id: self.group_id, user_id: target_assignee.id)
            self.assignee = target_assignee
          else
            assignee_group_mismatch = true
          end
        end
      end

      comment = if has_comment
        Comment.new(
          account: account,
          ticket: self,
          author: author,
          body: comment_attrs[:body],
          public: comment_attrs[:public]
        )
      end

      ticket_valid = valid?
      if group_invalid
        errors.add(:group_id, "is invalid")
        ticket_valid = false
      end
      if assignee_invalid
        errors.add(:assignee_id, "is invalid")
        ticket_valid = false
      end
      if assignee_group_mismatch
        errors.add(:assignee_id, "must belong to the ticket's group")
        ticket_valid = false
      end
      comment_valid = comment ? comment.valid? : true

      unless ticket_valid && comment_valid
        comment&.errors&.each do |error|
          next if error.attribute == :ticket
          errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
        end
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      customer_visible_change = (comment.present? && comment.public?) || will_save_change_to_status?

      now = Time.current
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      elsif will_save_change_to_status? || will_save_change_to_assignee_id? || will_save_change_to_priority? || will_save_change_to_group_id?
        self.updated_at = now
      end

      self.customer_updated_at = now if customer_visible_change
      save!

      reply_comment_to_deliver = comment if email_origin? && comment&.public?
    end

    if reply_comment_to_deliver
      TicketMailer.staff_reply(self, reply_comment_to_deliver).deliver_now
    end

    self
  end

  def apply_customer_update!(author:, has_comment:, comment_body:, has_status:, status:)
    unless has_comment || has_status
      errors.add(:base, "Comment or status is required")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
    end

    errors.clear

    target_status = if has_status
      if status.blank?
        errors.add(:status, :blank)
        nil
      elsif status == "solved" || (has_comment && status == "open")
        status
      else
        errors.add(:status, :inclusion)
        nil
      end
    else
      "open"
    end

    comment = if has_comment
      Comment.new(
        account: account,
        ticket: self,
        author: author,
        body: comment_body,
        public: true
      )
    end

    if comment && !comment.valid?
      comment.errors.each do |error|
        next if error.attribute == :ticket
        errors.add(:"comment.#{error.attribute}", error.message)
      end
    end

    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self) if errors.any?

    self.class.transaction do
      now = Time.current
      self.status = target_status
      if comment
        comment.created_at = now
        comment.updated_at = now
        comment.save!
        self.updated_at = now
      elsif will_save_change_to_status?
        self.updated_at = now
      end
      self.customer_updated_at = now if comment || will_save_change_to_status?
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: customer_updated_at
    }
  end

  def as_ticket_json
    {

      priority: priority,

      },

        id: group.id,
        name: group.name
      } : nil,

      assignee: assignee ? {
        id: assignee.id,

      } : nil,

      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  private

  def ensure_reply_token

  def parse_record_id_value(raw_id)

module Api
  module V1
    class GroupsController < BaseController
      before_action :authenticate_user!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_staff!, only: [:index, :show]
      before_action :require_admin!, only: [:create, :update, :destroy]
      before_action :load_group!, only: [:show, :update, :destroy]

      def index
        scope = current_account.groups.ordered
        render json: paginate(scope, resource_key: :groups, &:as_api_json), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        render json: { group: @group.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def create
        group_params = require_object_param(:group)

        group = Group.create_for_account!(
          account: current_account,
          name: scalar_string(group_params[:name])
        )

        render json: { group: group.as_api_json }, status: :created
      end

      def update
        group_params = require_object_param(:group)
        @group.rename!(scalar_string(group_params[:name]))

        render json: { group: @group.as_api_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def destroy
        @group.destroy_with_cleanup!
        head :no_content

module Api
  module V1
    class TicketsController < BaseController
      before_action :authenticate_user!
      before_action :require_active_account!
      before_action :require_staff!
      before_action :load_ticket!, only: [:show, :update]

      def index
        scope = current_account.tickets.includes(:requester, :assignee, :group).recently_active

        if params.key?(:status) && !params[:status].nil? && params[:status] != ""
          status = scalar_string(params[:status])
          unless status && Ticket::STATUSES.include?(status)
            render json: {
              error: "Status is not included in the list",
              errors: { status: ["is not included in the list"] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_content
            return
          end
          scope = scope.where(status: status)
        end

        if params.key?(:priority) && !params[:priority].nil? && params[:priority] != ""
          priority = scalar_string(params[:priority])
          unless priority && Ticket::PRIORITIES.include?(priority)
            render json: {
              error: "Priority is not included in the list",
              errors: { priority: ["is not included in the list"] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_content
            return
          end
          scope = scope.where(priority: priority)
        end

        if params.key?(:group_id) && !params[:group_id].nil? && params[:group_id] != ""
          if params[:group_id] == "unassigned"
            scope = scope.where(group_id: nil)
          else
            group_id = parse_record_id(params[:group_id])
            unless group_id
              render json: {
                error: "Group is invalid",
                errors: { group_id: ["is invalid"] }
              }, status: :unprocessable_content
              return
            end
            scope = scope.where(group_id: group_id)
          end
        end

        if params.key?(:assignee_id) && !params[:assignee_id].nil? && params[:assignee_id] != ""
          if params[:assignee_id] == "unassigned"
            scope = scope.where(assignee_id: nil)
          else
            assignee_id = parse_record_id(params[:assignee_id])
            unless assignee_id
              render json: {
                error: "Assignee is invalid",
                errors: { assignee_id: ["is invalid"] }
              }, status: :unprocessable_content
              return
            end
            scope = scope.where(assignee_id: assignee_id)
          end
        end

        if params.key?(:requester_id) && !params[:requester_id].nil? && params[:requester_id] != ""
          requester_id = parse_record_id(params[:requester_id])
          unless requester_id
            render json: {
              error: "Requester is invalid",
              errors: { requester_id: ["is invalid"] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_content
            return
          end
          scope = scope.where(requester_id: requester_id)
        end

        if params.key?(:q) && !params[:q].nil?
          raw_q = scalar_string(params[:q])
          if raw_q.nil?
            render json: {
              error: "Query is invalid",
              errors: { q: ["is invalid"] }
            }, status: :unprocessable_content
            return
          end
          query = raw_q.gsub(/\A[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+\z/, "")
          scope = scope.matching_query(query) unless query.empty?
        end

        render json: paginate(scope, resource_key: :tickets, &:as_ticket_json), status: :ok
      end

      def show
        render json: { ticket: @ticket.as_ticket_json }, status: :ok
      end

      def update
        ticket_params = require_object_param(:ticket)
        has_comment = ticket_params.key?(:comment)
        raw_comment = ticket_params[:comment]
        comment_attrs = if raw_comment.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
          {
            body: scalar_string(raw_comment[:body]),
            public: extract_boolean_param(raw_comment, :public, default: true)
          }
        else
          { body: nil, public: true }
        end
        has_status = ticket_params.key?(:status)
        status = has_status ? scalar_string(ticket_params[:status]) : nil
        has_assignee = ticket_params.key?(:assignee_id)
        raw_assignee_id = has_assignee ? ticket_params[:assignee_id] : nil
        has_priority = ticket_params.key?(:priority)
        priority = has_priority ? scalar_string(ticket_params[:priority]) : nil
        has_group = ticket_params.key?(:group_id)
        raw_group_id = has_group ? ticket_params[:group_id] : nil

        @ticket.apply_staff_update!(
          author: current_user,
          has_comment: has_comment,
          comment_attrs: comment_attrs,
          has_status: has_status,
          status: status,
          has_assignee: has_assignee,
          raw_assignee_id: raw_assignee_id,
          has_priority: has_priority,
          priority: priority,
          has_group: has_group,
          raw_group_id: raw_group_id
        )

        render json: { ticket: @ticket.as_ticket_json }, status: :ok
      end

      private

      def load_ticket!
        id = parse_record_id(params[:id])
        @ticket = id && current_account.tickets.includes(:requester, :assignee, :group).find_by(id: id)
        return if @ticket

        render json: { error: "Ticket not found" }, status: :not_found
      end
    end
  end

require "test_helper"
require "rake"

class GroupsAndRoutingTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    ENV.delete("HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL")
    ENV.delete("HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM")
  end

  def json_body
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def extract_link_params(mail, expected_path)
    body = mail.body.decoded
    match = body.match(%r{(https?://[^\s"<>]+)})
    assert match, "Expected URL in email body, got: #{body.inspect}"
    uri = URI.parse(match[1])
    assert_equal expected_path, uri.path
    [uri, URI.decode_www_form(uri.query).to_h]
  end

  def setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password")
    post "/api/v1/account/create",
      params: {
        account: {
          name: name,
          subdomain: subdomain,
          admin: { name: admin_name, email: email, password: password }
        }
      },
      as: :json
    assert_response :created
    owner = json_body.fetch("user")
    _uri, query = extract_link_params(ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last, "/verify-email")

    post "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm",
      params: { email_verification: { token: query.fetch("token") } },
      headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => subdomain },
      as: :json
    assert_response :ok
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
    owner
  end

  def auth_headers(subdomain, token)

  test "group CRUD, rename, ID ascending order, pagination, uniqueness, and role permissions" do
    setup_business!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", admin_name: "Jo", email: "jo@acme.test")
    setup_business!(subdomain: "globex", name: "Globex", admin_name: "Gus", email: "gus@globex.test")

    owner_headers = auth_headers("acme", sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: "my-first-password"))
    globex_headers = auth_headers("globex", sign_in!(subdomain: "globex", email: "gus@globex.test", password: "my-first-password"))

    alex = invite_and_accept_staff!(subdomain: "acme", owner_headers: owner_headers, email: "alex@acme.test", name: "Alex", role: "admin")

    sam_headers = auth_headers("acme", sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "sam@acme.test", password: "staff-password"))
    avery_headers = auth_headers("acme", sign_in!(subdomain: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: "my-customer-password"))

    # Admin creates groups; whitespace is stripped
    post "/api/v1/groups",
      params: { group: { name: "  Billing  " } },

      as: :json
    assert_response :unprocessable_content

    # Staff (both admin and agent) can list groups in ID ascending order (even after billing was updated later!) and inspect detail

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal 3, json_body["count"]
    assert_equal 2, json_body["next_page"]
    assert_equal [billing["id"], tech_support["id"]], json_body.fetch("groups").map { |g| g["id"] }

    get "/api/v1/groups/#{tech_support["id"]}", headers: sam_headers
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "Technical Support", json_body.dig("group", "name")

    # Agent cannot create, rename, or delete groups; customer cannot even browse groups
    post "/api/v1/groups", params: { group: { name: "VIP" } }, headers: sam_headers, as: :json
    assert_response :forbidden

    patch "/api/v1/groups/#{billing["id"]}", params: { group: { name: "Hacked" } }, headers: sam_headers, as: :json

    delete "/api/v1/groups/#{onboarding["id"]}", headers: sam_headers
    assert_response :forbidden

    get "/api/v1/groups", headers: avery_headers
    assert_response :forbidden

**A Nifty NUL Byte Discovery and a System-Wide Audit**

Aha! That test, specifically using `"Bad\u0000Name"`, brilliantly snagged a PostgreSQL `ArgumentError: string contains null byte`! It's clear that `group.valid?` was the culprit for throwing that error. And now the critical question is why?

The root cause? That pesky `validates :name, uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false }` validation! It was running a SQL `SELECT 1 FROM groups WHERE LOWER(groups.name) = LOWER('Bad\u0000Name')` even *after* a `format: { without: /\u0000/ }` validation already failed! The issue, of course, is that the `uniqueness` validation *shouldn't* query the database in the face of a failed format validation. The solution, therefore, is to include an `unless` condition like `unless: -> { name.to_s.include?("\u0000") }` (or potentially `!errors.include?(:name)`) within the `uniqueness` validation itself.

Fantastic! This edge case testing with NUL bytes paid off immediately. Now, I need to fix `app/models/group.rb` to prevent this from happening in the future. I'll add that `unless` condition to the `uniqueness` validation, ensuring the SQL query only executes if the `name` attribute doesn't contain a NUL byte.

But wait a moment... Before I rush to fix just that file, I must conduct a thorough audit. Could *any* other model within the codebase be susceptible to sending a NUL byte to PostgreSQL?

*   `Group#name`: Fixed! The `unless` condition on the `uniqueness` validator is the key.
*   `GroupMembership`: The `group_id` and `user_id` attributes are validated as integers using `/\A\d+\z/`, and the `default` is boolean. This is secure from NUL bytes.
*   `Ticket`: `group_id` and `assignee_id` are also validated as integers, and `status` and `priority` rely on `STATUSES` and `PRIORITIES` Ruby arrays, meaning no SQL injection is possible.

Okay, with a clean bill of health across the entire codebase, I can confidently update `app/models/group.rb` and re-run those tests. The system is now more robust against these potential injection attacks.

class Group < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  has_many :group_memberships, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :users, through: :group_memberships
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :nullify

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.is_a?(String) ? value.strip : value }

  validates :name,
    presence: true,
    format: { without: /\u0000/ }
  validates :name,
    uniqueness: { scope: :account_id, case_sensitive: false },
    unless: -> { name.blank? || name.include?("\u0000") }

  scope :ordered, -> { order(id: :asc) }

  def self.create_for_account!(account:, name:)
    group = account.groups.new(name: name)

    account.with_lock do
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(group) unless group.valid?
      group.save!
    end

    group
  end

  def rename!(new_name)
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      self.name = new_name
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self) unless valid?
      save!
    end

    self
  end

  def destroy_with_cleanup!
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      affected_user_ids = group_memberships.where(default: true).pluck(:user_id)

      account.tickets.where(group_id: id).update_all(group_id: nil, assignee_id: nil)
      group_memberships.delete_all
      destroy!

      affected_user_ids.each do |uid|
        next if account.group_memberships.where(user_id: uid, default: true).exists?

        replacement = account.group_memberships.where(user_id: uid).ordered.first
        replacement&.update!(default: true)
      end
    end
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      account_id: account_id,
      name: name,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end

require "net/http"
require "json"
require "uri"

pid = spawn(
  { "PORT" => "3210", "RAILS_ENV" => "development" },
  "bin/rails", "server", "-p", "3210",
  out: "/tmp/puma_verify.log",
  err: "/tmp/puma_verify.log"
)

begin
  20.times do
    res = Net::HTTP.get_response(URI("http://127.0.0.1:3210/up")) rescue nil
    break if res && res.code == "200"
    sleep 0.25
  end

  def req(method, path, body: nil, headers: {})
    uri = URI("http://127.0.0.1:3210#{path}")
    http = Net::HTTP.new(uri.host, uri.port)
    klass = {
      get: Net::HTTP::Get,
      post: Net::HTTP::Post,
      patch: Net::HTTP::Patch,
      put: Net::HTTP::Put,
      delete: Net::HTTP::Delete
    }.fetch(method)
    r = klass.new(uri)
    headers.each { |k, v| r[k] = v }
    if body
      r["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
      r.body = JSON.generate(body)
    end
    res = http.request(r)
    [res.code.to_i, res.body.to_s.empty? ? nil : JSON.parse(res.body)]
  end

  code, data = req(:post, "/api/v1/account/create", body: {
    account: {
      name: "Smoke Corp",
      subdomain: "smokecorp",
      admin: { name: "Admin", email: "admin@smokecorp.test", password: "secret-password" }
    }
  })
  raise "Create failed: #{code} #{data}" unless code == 201
  admin_id = data.dig("user", "id")

  # Verify admin directly via runner for quick smoke check
  system("bin/rails runner '\''Account.find_by!(subdomain: \"smokecorp\").users.first.verify_email!'\''") or raise "verify failed"

  code, sdata = req(:post, "/api/v1/sessions",
    headers: { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "smokecorp" },
    body: { session: { email: "admin@smokecorp.test", password: "secret-password" } }
  )
  raise "Session failed: #{code}" unless code == 201
  h = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "smokecorp", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{sdata.dig("session", "token")}" }

  code, gdata = req(:post, "/api/v1/groups", headers: h, body: { group: { name: "Billing" } })
  raise "Group create failed: #{code}" unless code == 201
  gid = gdata.dig("group", "id")

  code, mdata = req(:post, "/api/v1/group_memberships", headers: h, body: {
    group_membership: { group_id: gid, user_id: admin_id, default: true }
  })
  raise "Membership create failed: #{code}" unless code == 201
  mid = mdata.dig("group_membership", "id")

  code, _ = req(:put, "/api/v1/group_memberships/#{mid}/make_default", headers: h)
  raise "make_default failed: #{code}" unless code == 200

  code, _ = req(:delete, "/api/v1/groups/#{gid}", headers: h)
  raise "Group delete failed: #{code}" unless code == 204

  puts "LIVE PUMA SMOKE TEST PASSED!"
ensure
  Process.kill("TERM", pid) rescue nil
  Process.wait(pid) rescue nil
  File.delete("/tmp/puma_verify.log") if File.exist?("/tmp/puma_verify.log")
  system("bin/rails runner '\''Account.where(subdomain: \"smokecorp\").destroy_all'\''")
end
'

I have implemented groups, group memberships, default group management, inbox group filtering, and group-aware ticket assignment rules:

- **Schema & Models (`Group`, `GroupMembership`, `Ticket`, `Account`, `User`)**:
  - Added `groups` (with account-scoped case-insensitive name uniqueness and ID-ascending ordering), `group_memberships` (enforcing unique `(group_id, user_id)` pairs and a partial unique index ensuring at most one `default` membership per user), and `tickets.group_id`.
  - Automatically ensures every staff member with memberships has exactly one default membership when adding memberships, switching defaults, or deleting memberships/groups.
  - Cleans up invalid ticket assignments when groups or memberships are deleted while preserving group memberships across staff suspension/unsuspension.
- **API Endpoints (`Api::V1::GroupsController`, `Api::V1::GroupMembershipsController`, `Api::V1::TicketsController`)**:
  - Added `GET /api/v1/groups`, `GET /api/v1/groups/:id`, `POST /api/v1/groups`, `PATCH /api/v1/groups/:id`, and `DELETE /api/v1/groups/:id` (browsable by staff, mutable by admins, ordered by ID ascending).
  - Added `GET /api/v1/group_memberships` (filterable by `group_id` and `user_id`, ordered by ID ascending), `GET /api/v1/group_memberships/:id`, `POST /api/v1/group_memberships`, `DELETE /api/v1/group_memberships/:id`, and `PUT /api/v1/group_memberships/:id/make_default`.
  - Extended ticket serialization with `group_id` and `group` (`{ id, name }` or `nil`), inbox filtering by `group_id` or `group_id=unassigned`, and ticket assignment/routing rules (requiring assignees to belong to the ticket's group, using the assignee's default group when assigning an ungrouped ticket, clearing incompatible assignees when moving groups, keeping the group when clearing the assignee, and clearing the assignee when explicitly clearing the group).
- **Tests (`test/integration/groups_and_routing_test.rb`)**:
  - Added comprehensive integration tests covering CRUD, permissions, defaults, inbox filters, ticket routing, deletions, suspension, multi-tenancy, account purge, and malformed inputs.

Let's now complete the task and submit the final output.
